# Volume 3 — Chapter X Tabby’s Place

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The following evening, they were walking with determination along the herringbone path that crossed the small garden. The April wind was causing the pines to sing their song, while the grove teemed with robins—large, fat, bold creatures, swaggering on the walkways. The girls pressed the doorbell with some hesitation, and a stern, elderly maid let them in. Entering through the door brought them straight into a spacious living room, in which two additional ladies, both equally stern and elderly, were seated beside a bright, small fire. Aside from the fact that one appeared to be roughly seventy and the other fifty, there appeared to be small variation between the two. Both possessed remarkably large, pale-blue eyes behind steel-framed glasses; both were wearing a cap and a gray shawl; both were knitting continuously at an unhurried pace; both were rocking calmly and eyeing the girls in silence; and positioned directly behind both was a big white china dog, covered in circular green spots, with a green nose and green ears. Those dogs instantly caught Nell’s imagination; to her, they appeared to be the dual protective spirits of Tabby’s Place.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0000 }

Silence reigned among everyone for a brief period. Speech eluded the girls because of their anxiety, while the old ladies and the china dogs appeared equally uncommunicative. Nell looked around at her surroundings. How charming the place was! From it, a second door led straight to the pine grove, where robins fearlessly approached the actual step. Scattered across the floor were circular braided rugs, identical to those Thirza constructed at Grey Shutters, though such items were deemed obsolete anywhere else, Brierley included. Nevertheless, they were present right here on Linden Avenue! Positioned in a corner, a large, gleaming grandfather’s clock made loud, solemn ticking sounds. Above the mantelpiece sat charming small cupboards, their glass doors revealing shiny, curious pieces of china. Old prints together with silhouettes adorned the walls. The staircase ascended in a corner, featuring a wide window paired with an attractive seat at its initial low landing. Everything corresponded precisely to what Nell was certain it would be.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0001 }

At this point the quiet had become exceedingly unbearable, so Honora gave Nell a nudge to signify that she ought to talk.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0002 }

“By your notice, we—we—observed that this dwelling is available for rent,” Nell uttered weakly to the senior woman, who clearly was Miss Tabby Linden.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0003 }

“Oh, yes,” Miss Tabby stated. “It was my intention to remove that sign today.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0004 }

“Then—in that case we are late,” Nell said mournfully. “Has it been let to another person?”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0005 }

“No, but we have made a decision that it will not be let under any circumstances.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0006 }

“Oh, I’m so sorry,” Nell blurted out spontaneously. “I love this place so much. I really hoped we might have secured it.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0007 }

At that moment, Miss Tabby set her knitting aside, removed her spectacles, wiped them clean, placed them back on, and peered at Nell as a fellow person for the very first time. The second woman mirrored her actions with such exactness that she could easily have passed for an image in a looking glass.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0008 }

“You love it,” Miss Tabby stated forcefully. “Does that signify that your affection for it is genuine? Or does it simply imply that its appearance pleases you? Young women these days make such extravagant assertions that a person can never determine what they actually intend to say. Things were different when I was young. Back then, a girl would not declare her love for turnips using the exact same tone she could have employed to declare her love for her mother or her Savior.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0009 }

Her conscience gave Nell strength.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0010 }

“I truly do adore it,” she spoke softly. “Ever since I spotted it previous autumn, I have adored it. Next year, my two college buddies and I wish to manage a home rather than live in a boarding house, which is why we are searching for a small property to lease; and I felt so joyful upon seeing that this residence was available to rent.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0011 }

“You are welcome to take it, provided you love it,” Miss Tabby stated. “Maria and I made up our minds today against renting it after all, since none of the individuals who desired it appealed to us. Renting it is not something we are forced to do. Our trip to Europe remains affordable for us even without leasing it. Although it would assist us financially, no amount of money could convince me to surrender my home to the kinds of people who have visited and viewed it. Your case is not the same. It is my belief that you truly love it and will treat it well. It is yours to have.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0012 }

“If—if we are able to pay the price you demand,” Nell faltered.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0013 }

The necessary sum was stated by Miss Tabby. A mutual look was exchanged between Nell and Honora. A shake of her head came from Honora.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0014 }

“I fear we are unable to pay that high a price,” Nell remarked, suppressing her letdown. “You see, we happen to be merely college girls, and our funds are limited.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0015 }

“How much did you imagine you were able to pay?” asked Miss Tabby, without pausing in her knitting.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0016 }

Nell stated how much she wanted. Miss Tabby gave a serious nod.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0017 }

“That will suffice. As I previously mentioned to you, renting it out is not absolutely required for us. Though we lack wealth, our means are sufficient for a trip to Europe. I myself have never set foot in Europe, nor did I ever anticipate or desire such a journey. However, my niece over there, Maria Linden, has developed a desire to travel there. Surely you understand that a youth such as Maria is unable to travel the world by herself.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0018 }

“No—I—I suppose not,” muttered Nell, observing that Miss Tabby was completely and seriously sincere.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0019 }

“Certainly not. Therefore, I must accompany her to take care of her. I anticipate liking it as well; my age is seventy years, yet I am not weary of life so far. It is likely I would have traveled to Europe earlier had I thought of it. Our absence will last for two years, maybe three. Our departure by ship is in June, at which time we will mail you the key and arrange everything so you can move in whenever you decide. A few items that we value particularly will be packed up by us, but everything else is going to remain.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0020 }

“Are you going to leave the china dogs behind?” Nell inquired with hesitation.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0021 }

“Do you want me to?”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0022 }

“Oh, truly, yes. They are charming.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0023 }

Miss Tabby’s face took on a satisfied look.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0024 }

“Those dogs mean a lot to me,” she boasted. “Their age exceeds one hundred years, and their positions on both flanks of this hearth have remained unchanged from the time my brother Aaron fetched them from London half a century back. My brother Aaron was the namesake for Linden Avenue.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0025 }

“He was a fine man,” Miss Maria stated, offering her initial remark. “Ah, his equal cannot be found these days.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0026 }

“Maria, to you he was a good uncle,” Miss Tabby said, showing clear emotion. “Remembering him is the right thing for you to do.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0027 }

“I will never forget him,” Miss Maria remarked with gravity. “In my mind's eye, I see him right now, positioned in front of the hearth with his hands tucked beneath his coat-tails, smiling warmly at us.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0028 }

Miss Maria produced her handkerchief to dry her eyes, yet Miss Tabby returned with determination from sentimental matters to those of a practical nature.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0029 }

“Provided you pledge to take great care of the dogs, I am going to leave them in their current spots,” she stated. “They are named Gog and Magog. Gog’s gaze goes toward the right, whereas Magog’s goes toward the left. Furthermore, I have a final query. It isn't a problem for you, I trust, if this house goes by the name of Tabby’s Place?”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0030 }

“No, truly. It seems to us that this represents one of its most delightful aspects.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0031 }

“I observe that you possess good sense,” Miss Tabby remarked with an air of deep gratification. “Can you imagine? Every single person who arrived to lease this residence inquired whether removing the gate’s name while they resided here was permissible. I informed them firmly that the property and its name were inseparable. From the moment my brother Aaron bequeathed this property to me, it has been known as Tabby’s Place, and Tabby’s Place it will continue to be called until my death and Maria’s death. Once those occur, whoever inherits it next is free to give it whatever absurd title pleases him,” Miss Tabby finished, in a manner quite similar to saying, “After that—the deluge.” “Now, prior to treating our agreement as finalized, would you care to tour the residence and inspect everything?”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0032 }

Continued searching brought the girls even more joy. A kitchen and a little bedroom were located on the lower floor, in addition to the spacious living-room. Three bedrooms were situated on the upper floor, consisting of one big room and two little ones. A particular small room, which looked out toward the massive pines, captivated Nell, and she wished for it to belong to her. Its walls were covered in light blue wallpaper, and it contained a tiny, vintage vanity table equipped with candle sconces. A window with diamond-shaped panes featured a bench beneath its light blue muslin drapes, offering an ideal place to study or daydream.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0033 }

“Everything is so wonderful that I am certain we will awaken to discover it was merely a passing dream,” Honora stated while they departed.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0034 }

“Miss Tabby and Miss Maria do not seem like the material that dreams are created from,” Nell chuckled. “Could you imagine them traveling around the world—particularly wearing those caps and shawls?”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0035 }

“I imagine that once they start moving at a genuine trot, they will set them down,” remarked Honora, “yet I am certain that they will carry their knitting wherever they go. It would be impossible for them to leave it behind. I am convinced they will wander around Westminster Abbey while continuing to knit. In the time between, Nell, we will reside in Tabby’s Place—as well as on Linden Avenue. Already, I feel as if I were a millionairess.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0036 }

“I feel as though I am a morning star singing with delight,” Nell declared.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0037 }

Cressy Lindsay tiptoed into Thirty-eight, St. John’s, during that night and threw herself onto the bed belonging to Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0038 }

“My darlings, I am utterly exhausted. My situation brings to mind the person who lacked a homeland—or perhaps he lacked a shadow? I cannot recall which one. At any rate, my time has been spent packing.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0039 }

“And I assume your exhaustion comes from being unable to choose what to pack first, or deciding where to place them,” Honora laughed.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0040 }

“Precisely. Furthermore, once I had managed to stuff all my belongings inside, and both my landlady and her maid sat atop it as I secured the lock, I realized that numerous items needed for Convocation were stowed at the absolute bottom. Unlocking the ancient trunk became necessary, requiring an hour of rummaging and probing to retrieve the desired objects. I would grasp an item that seemed to be the right one, pull it out, and find it was a different article entirely. Indeed, Nell, I refrained from swearing.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0041 }

“I never claimed that you had done so.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0042 }

“Indeed, your appearance reflected it. Yet I confess that my own reflections bordered on the blasphemous. Furthermore, my head cold is so severe that my actions are limited entirely to sniffling, sighing, and sneezing. Does that not strike you as alliterative torment? Queen Nell, I beg you to utter something that might raise my spirits.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0043 }

“Bear in mind that on the coming Thursday evening, you will return to the realm of Hector and Orlando,” Nell proposed.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0044 }

Cressy gave a sorrowful shake of her head.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0045 }

“Further use of alliteration. No, Hector and Orlando are not what I desire when my head is stuffed with a cold. However, what has occurred with the pair of you? Now that my gaze is fixed upon you attentively, you appear entirely illuminated by an inner radiance. Why, you are literally glowing! What is going on?”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0046 }

“In the coming winter, we will be residing at Tabby’s Place,” Nell declared with a triumphant air. “Take note, we will actually live there rather than board! It has been rented by us, with Mabel Colby joining our household and her aunt taking on the housekeeping duties for us.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0047 }

Jumping up, Cressy dried her nose, after which she dropped to her knees in front of Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0048 }

“Girls—girls—allow me to accompany you, too. Oh, my behavior will be so wonderful. Should you lack space for me, my bed will be the small kennel situated in the orchard—I have observed it. Just permit me to join.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0049 }

“Rise, you goose.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0050 }

“I will not rise from my knees until you assure me that I may reside with you during the coming winter.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0051 }

Nell exchanged a glance with Honora. After that, Nell spoke deliberately, “We would be delighted to host you, Cressy dear. However, it is best to be honest with one another. My means are limited—Nonie lacks money too—and Mabel Colby has little wealth—consequently, our home management must be extremely modest and our food unpretentious. Your lifestyle would need to match ours. As it stands, you possess fortune, and your boardinghouse meals prove it.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0052 }

“Oh, why should that matter to me?” asked Cressy dramatically. “It is far superior to share a simple meal of herbs alongside your friends than to eat a fattened ox in an isolated boardinghouse. Do not assume that I care only for my belly, girls. I would happily survive on mere bread and water—accompanied by just a tiny bit of jam—provided you allow me to join you.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0053 }

“And after that,” Nell went on, “a lot of labor will need to be accomplished. The aunt of Mabel is unable to handle everything. Each of us anticipates having tasks to perform. As for you—”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0054 }

“Neither do I spin, nor do I toil,” Cressida concluded. “However, I will get the hang of tasks. Demonstrating them to me a single time will be sufficient. Starting off, making my own bed is within my ability. Moreover, keep in mind that even if cooking is beyond me, holding my temper is not. That counts for something. Furthermore, complaining about the weather is something I never do. That counts for even more. Oh, I beg you, I beg you! My desire for anything has never been this strong in all my days—and how terribly hard this floor feels.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0055 }

“There is only one additional matter,” stated Honora with determination. “As the whole of Wexcombe is aware, you, Cressy, receive visitors nearly every night. However, at Tabby’s Place that will not be permitted for us. It has been settled that Friday nights are the sole times we will receive our acquaintances. Should you join us, you must conform to that regulation.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0056 }

“Well, you surely don't imagine I'll object to that, do you? Why, it pleases me. I was aware that I ought to have established a similar regulation on my own, but I lacked sufficient resolve to create it or adhere to it. Being able to shift this burden onto your shoulders will provide genuine comfort. Should you refuse to allow me to share your fate, the sorrow will kill me, and subsequently I shall return to disturb you. I shall make my home right upon the threshold of Tabby’s Place, making it impossible for you to enter or leave without tripping across my ghost.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0057 }

Once more, expressive glances passed between Nell and Honora.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0058 }

“Well,” Nell remarked, “naturally, our ability to bring you along depends on speaking with Mabel first; nevertheless, I doubt she will have any objections, and speaking for ourselves, you are free to join us with a warm reception.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0059 }

“If you grow weary of our humble existence you are free to depart from us, without being questioned,” Honora appended.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0060 }

Cressy leapt to her feet, gave a joyful hug to the pair, and continued on her path with delight.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0061 }

“I wish that everything turns out well,” Honora remarked with gravity.
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0062 }

“We have to force them to head right,” declared Nell. “It seems to me that Cressy is going to suit our ’appy little ’ome extremely well.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0063 }

“Oh, Cressy is wonderful to hang out with and be good friends. And, naturally, having more people in our group will lighten the burden on our small budgets. However, what will it be like sharing a home with her? A person must be experienced through summer and winter before you can determine whether she is agreeable to live with or not.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0064 }

“Oh, well, every one of us will be put to the test, for that matter. And we need to conduct ourselves like reasonable people, living and letting live. Cressy is not selfish, even if she is somewhat thoughtless, and I think that all of us will get along wonderfully in Tabby’s Place.”
{: #nw-v03-c10-p0065 }
